If your CSV has one row per date and columns rank1..rank10:
```
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('namebeam_ai_visibility_wide.csv')
url_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.lower().startswith('rank') or 'url' in c.lower()]
all_urls = pd.Series(df[url_cols].values.ravel()).dropna().astype(str).str.strip()
unique_pages = all_urls.unique()
print(len(unique_pages))
```

Normalization tips: consider lowercasing, removing UTM/query params, and trimming trailing slashes if you want to treat those as the same page:
```
from urllib.parse import urlparse, urlunparse, parse_qs
def normalize(u):
    try:
        p = urlparse(u)
        # drop query params:
        cleaned = urlunparse((p.scheme, p.netloc, p.path.rstrip('/'), '', '', ''))
        return cleaned.lower()
    except:
        return u.strip().lower()
all_norm = all_urls.apply(normalize)
print(len(all_norm.unique()))
```
